summary: IBM's personal computer, model 5150, built quickly from off-the-shelf parts with an open design. That openness let other companies clone it, and the “IBM compatible” became the standard that today's PCs still descend from.

image.alt: IBM Personal Computer 5150 with its monitor and keyboard

events.note: IBM introduces the model 5150 at a base price of US$1,565.

events.label: First clone
events.note: Columbia Data Products sells the first legal PC-compatible clone.

events.label: PC XT
events.note: Adds a hard drive as standard.

events.label: PC AT
events.note: Moves to the faster Intel 80286 processor.
IBM discontinues the PC line and introduces the PS/2.

cause: The model was discontinued, but its design became the standard every clone followed.
